items.title: Bill Watrous interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 26, 1999
items.q: I used to watch how he would keep his corners down when he played, and how gracefully he moved the slide.

ctx.x: Not the best thing for a smooth slide.

No. He was understanding about it. He never really gave me much attitude about it. And so I just simply developed on my own. I can’t recall him taking any active part except to criticize, that was his role, was to be critical. “Oh your mouthpiece isn’t positioned properly” blah-blah-blah-blah. “You’re using too much pressure” or this, that and the other thing, the little things, and I used to watch how he would keep his corners down when he played, and how gracefully he moved the slide. There weren’t any jerky…

Yeah. You know I have this recollection, I was either in college or around then and a bunch of my musician friends were watching a show that you were on. I can’t recall what it was. But they had this very close-up thing and like we just were in awe. First of all what you were playing, the range and so forth, but that it seemed to effortless and immovable. No gyrations.
